basis: Requirements-first model written from PRODUCT.md, ROADMAP.md, BACKLOG.md, docs/ux-implementation/dibayar-implementation-spec.md, SPEC_RECONCILIATION.md, docs/validation/M4-READINESS.md, SECURITY.md, CLAUDE.md and issues #53/#55, before the UI was inspected. Proposed by the 2026-10-17 completeness audit; every classification is a proposal for the product owner (Chris) to confirm or change.
rules: This file is the list of what a creator must be able to do. It is maintained by hand and does not follow the UI or docs/testing/journey-coverage.json: removing or re-marking an inventory action cannot make a capability disappear.

REQUIRED: an explicit product requirement, or indispensable to the target creator's core outcome. PROPOSED: a plausible improvement that needs a product-owner decision. NOT_APPLICABLE: outside scope or excluded by a business rule. UNKNOWN: not enough evidence; the owner decides and nobody builds it in the meantime.

A REQUIRED capability is covered when every inventory action it maps to exists, is applicable, and is automated_real_interaction or manual_verified, or is held by a release gate in the inventory's exception register. A REQUIRED capability that is not covered must carry a gap with an issue (#N) or a finding (FIND-N). A gap on a covered capability is stale and fails the check.
Pinned tests (`verification.tests`) must stay listed under the named inventory action; npm run coverage:journeys proves each listed test is registered and not skipped.
Reclassifying a capability needs a rationale entry naming the decision and who made it.
